gloss: to break into a run; to run out; to dash off

forms.label: Past polite
forms.negative: {駆|か}け{出|だ}しませんでした

forms.label: ている past
forms.negative: {駆|か}け{出|だ}していなかった

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {駆|か}け{出|だ}していませんでした

definitions.gloss: to break into a run; to start running; to dash off
definitions.explanation: To suddenly begin running, often triggered by urgency, excitement, or alarm.

definitions.gloss: to run out (of a place); to rush out
definitions.explanation: To run out from inside a building or enclosed space.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}たちが{駆|か}け{出|だ}した。
examples.english: The children broke into a run.

examples.japanese: ベルが{鳴|な}ると、{生徒|せいと}たちは{教室|きょうしつ}から{駆|か}け{出|だ}した。
examples.english: When the bell rang, the students ran out of the classroom.

examples.japanese: {急|きゅう}に{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}り{出|だ}したので、{軒下|のきした}に{向|む}かって{駆|か}け{出|だ}した。
examples.english: It suddenly started raining, so I dashed toward the eaves.

examples.japanese: {犬|いぬ}が{玄関|げんかん}のドアから{駆|か}け{出|だ}して{行|い}った。
examples.english: The dog ran out through the front door.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{知|し}らせを{聞|き}くと、{椅子|いす}から{立|た}ち{上|あ}がって{駆|か}け{出|だ}した。
examples.english: When he heard the news, he jumped up from his chair and dashed off.

examples.japanese: {地震|じしん}で{建物|たてもの}が{揺|ゆ}れ、{人々|ひとびと}は{外|そと}に{駆|か}け{出|だ}した。
examples.english: The building shook from the earthquake, and people rushed outside.

notes:
COMMON PATTERNS:
{駆|か}け{出|だ}す is a compound verb: {駆|か}ける (to run) + {出|だ}す (to start / to go out). The {出|だ}す component contributes either the meaning of "beginning" (sense 1) or "exiting" (sense 2).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {外|そと}に{駆|か}け{出|だ}す (to rush outside)
- {急|いそ}いで{駆|か}け{出|だ}す (to hurry out running)
- {家|いえ}を{飛|と}び{出|だ}す is similar but emphasizes leaving home abruptly

Godan verb (す row): {駆|か}け{出|だ}さない / {駆|か}け{出|だ}します / {駆|か}け{出|だ}して
